prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor room where the camera wearer holds a cell phone (brightest white, ~0.3–0.4 m away and within arm's reach) at the bottom-center in frames 1–3, beside a large cushion or armrest on the lower left (~0.5–0.8 m away). Across the carpeted floor (~1.5–2.5 m ahead), a terrarium/aquarium stand sits in the center-background (~2.5–3 m away) with a small side table and a wall-mounted TV to the right (~2 m away, separated from the stand by ~0.5–1 m), while a dark doorway area on the back-left is farthest away (near-black, >3.5 m). Between frames 3 and 5, the camera wearer pitches and pans their head upward and to the left as the phone drops out of the bottom of the frame, revealing a standing man in frame 5 at ~2–2.5 m distance in front of the back-left closet and doorway, holding a plate within his own arm's reach (~0.3 m from his torso) while facing and looking toward the camera wearer. The depth map clarifies the 3D geometry of the dark furniture silhouette beneath the terrarium and the continuous floor plane that are lost in shadow in the RGB strip, and preserves the room layout during the severe motion blur of frame 4. However, it is unreliable where the bright glass terrarium and TV screen flatten into the wall depth, and where the deep shadow in the back-left corner creates a sharp black depth discontinuity.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates key foreground and mid-ground objects across the room layout: the handheld `cell phone` at bottom-center (~0.3–0.4 m, within the camera wearer's reach) and the partially visible `tv` on the upper right (~2 m away, ~1.5 m above the floor) in frames 1–4. As the camera tilts up and turns left in frames 4 and 5, the `cell phone` and `tv` exit the view to the bottom and right, while a standing `person` (~2–2.5 m away, facing the camera wearer) is segmented in the upper-left doorway in frame 4 and center-right in frame 5, holding an object on his plate labeled `banana` within his right hand's reach (~2 m from the camera wearer, just left of his hip). This map helps separate the dark-clothed person from the dark doorway background during the heavy motion blur of frame 4 and highlights the small food item on the plate in frame 5. However, the map is unreliable in frame 3 where it misclassifies the inanimate lower-left cushion/armrest (~0.5–0.8 m away) as a `person`, completely misses the camera wearer's own knees/hands holding the phone, and leaves large structural elements like the terrarium stand, tables, and walls unsegmented. It also truncates the standing person's lower legs at the bottom frame boundary in frame 5 and clips the TV at the right boundary in frames 1–4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1–4, providing no spatial information about the room layout, the camera wearer's hands holding the phone within arm's reach (~0.3–0.4 m), or the blurred person entering on the left in frame 4. In frame 5, a single yellow body skeleton appears on the center-right for the standing person (~2–2.5 m from the camera wearer, in front of the back doorway and to the left of the terrarium), with his hips cut off near the bottom of the view. The skeleton's shoulder alignment and dense cluster of facial keypoints confirm his torso and head face directly toward the camera wearer, while his right arm extends downward and to the viewer's left (~0.3 m from his hip) to hold the plate and his left elbow bends sharply upward to place his left hand at his mouth. This skeleton makes the person's exact upper-body joint articulation—specifically the raised left arm occluded against his dark shirt—much clearer than in the dimly lit RGB frame alone. However, the map is unreliable prior to frame 5 due to missing the camera wearer's hands and legs in frames 1–3 and failing to detect the motion-blurred body in frame 4, and even in frame 5 it omits the magenta hand skeletons for both of the standing man's hands.
